core_obligations: Read (1) iff (2) off the universal property of the seminormalization (proof lines 12312-12314).
Derive (2) from (3) by applying (3) to the seminormalization morphism (proof lines 12314-12316).
Assume (2) and factor the identity through the universal homeomorphism of (3) (proof lines 12316-12322).
Show the first arrow is a closed immersion and hence an isomorphism, giving (3) (proof lines 12322-12327).
proof_roadmap: (1) iff (2) from the universal property (proof lines 12312-12314).
(2) implies (3) by factoring the identity (proof lines 12316-12327).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises seminormality of a scheme in three equivalent ways: the scheme is seminormal; it equals its own seminormalization; and every universal homeomorphism onto it which induces isomorphisms on residue fields and has reduced source is an isomorphism. The proof reads the equivalence of the first two off the construction of the seminormalization, derives the second from the third by applying it to the seminormalization morphism, and proves the third from the second by factoring the identity of the scheme through the assumed universal homeomorphism, showing the first arrow of that factorisation is a closed immersion using the section-immersion lemma and separatedness, and concluding it is an isomorphism because it is also bijective on points and its target is reduced.
